name: Spotify

composio.note: Composio has no default OAuth app for Spotify. You must register your own app in the Spotify Developer Dashboard and paste its client ID and secret into a Composio auth config. Your app's quota mode (Development vs Extended) decides who can connect.

verdict.headline: You can connect your own account in under an hour, but for most teams production access to Spotify isn't available at all.
verdict.summary: Creating an app is instant, but Development Mode caps each app at 5 allowlisted users, needs the owner to hold Spotify Premium, and since February 2026 limits which endpoints and fields you get. Extended Quota Mode, the only way to serve arbitrary users, is open only to registered organisations with at least 250k monthly active users, and review takes up to six weeks. Spotify's Developer Terms also forbid ingesting Spotify Content into an ML or AI model, which needs a legal read for any agent product.

toProduction.label: Not available unless you are an organisation with 250k+ MAU; then 2–6+ weeks after applying

activeEffort.label: 1–3 hours for dev mode; 1–3 days more to prepare a partner application

approval.name: Extended Quota Mode (Spotify Partner Application, then Quota Extension Request)
approval.trigger: Any user beyond the 5 allowlisted accounts in Development Mode, or any need for endpoints/fields removed from Development Mode in February 2026.
approval.wait: Up to six weeks per Spotify's docs. Only organisations meeting the criteria are accepted, so for small developers the realistic answer is 'not approved'.

prerequisites.text: A Spotify account with an active Premium subscription for the app owner. If Premium lapses, the Development Mode app stops working until you resubscribe.
Development Mode Client ID limit: was 1 per developer from February 2026; raised to 25 in July 2026.

For production (Extended Quota): a legally registered business or organisation, a launched service, at least 250k MAU, availability in key Spotify markets, commercial viability, and a company email address for the application.
Acceptance of the Spotify Developer Terms, including the ban on training or ingesting Spotify Content into ML/AI models.

oauth.refreshTokens: Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh tokens last 6 months from user authorization; refreshing does not extend that. A refresh response may or may not include a new refresh token, so keep the old one if none is returned. Expired or revoked tokens return `invalid_grant`; restart the auth flow.
oauth.redirectUriRules: Exact match with a URI registered on the app. HTTPS required, except loopback IP literals (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT`, `http://[::1]:PORT`) which may use HTTP. `localhost` is not allowed. Enforced for new apps from 9 April 2025; all clients expected to migrate by November 2025.

steps.title: Confirm the owner account has Spotify Premium
steps.detail: Development Mode apps only work while the owner has an active Premium subscription. Use an account the team controls, not a personal one that might lapse.

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Dashboard
steps.detail: Dashboard → **Create an App**. Enter an app name and description (both show on the consent screen), tick the Developer Terms checkbox, click **Create**. A human must sign in and accept the terms.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard: **Create Auth Config** → toolkit `SPOTIFY` → **OAuth2**. Copy the redirect URI the dashboard shows. Composio's guides for other apps show `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`; treat that as an example only and use what the dashboard displays.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI and copy credentials
steps.detail: In the Spotify app settings, add the Composio redirect URI exactly (HTTPS). For local testing use `http://127.0.0.1:PORT`, never `localhost`. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the app overview page and paste them into the Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Request only what your tools need, e.g. `user-read-playback-state`, `user-modify-playback-state`, `playlist-modify-private`, `user-library-read`. Composio's toolkit page lists the scope each tool requires. An agent can draft this list.

steps.title: Allowlist test users
steps.detail: In the app's **Users and Access** section, add each Spotify user (name + the email on their Spotify account). Max 5 per app. Community reports say this cannot be automated.

steps.title: Connect your own account and run a call
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, sign in with an allowlisted account, then call e.g. get current user or playback state. Check that the endpoints you need still exist for Development Mode apps (see the February 2026 migration guide).

steps.title: Review the Developer Terms for your use case
steps.detail: The terms ban using the platform or Spotify Content to train an ML/AI model or otherwise ingesting Spotify Content into one. Passing track metadata into an LLM prompt may fall under this. Get a legal read before shipping an agent feature.

steps.title: Apply for Extended Quota (organisations only)
steps.detail: Only if you meet all criteria (registered business, launched service, 250k+ MAU, key markets, commercial viability). Submit the Partner Application from a company email. If accepted, file a **Quota extension Request** in the dashboard.

steps.title: Wait for Spotify review
steps.detail: Spotify says review can take up to six weeks. Until approved, you stay at 5 users.

scopes.name: user-modify-playback-state
scopes.purpose: Control playback (Premium user needed for playback control)

scopes.name: user-read-email
scopes.purpose: Read email address. Note: the `email` field is removed from user objects for Development Mode apps since Feb 2026

gotchas.title: Production is gated on 250k MAU and a registered business
gotchas.detail: Since 15 May 2025 Spotify accepts Extended Quota applications only from organisations meeting all criteria, including at least 250k MAU. A new agent product cannot get there, so it stays at 5 users per app.

gotchas.title: Terms ban feeding Spotify Content into AI models
gotchas.detail: Developer Terms Section IV forbid using Spotify Content to train an ML/AI model or 'otherwise ingesting' it into one. This is directly relevant to LLM agents that read Spotify data.

gotchas.title: Development Mode lost endpoints and fields in February 2026
gotchas.detail: Batch fetches (`GET /tracks`, `/albums`, `/artists`...), new releases, browse categories, artist top tracks, other users' profiles/playlists and `GET /markets` were removed. Playlist `/tracks` became `/items`. Fields like `popularity`, `email`, `product`, `country` were dropped. Search `limit` max is 10. Older tutorials and SDKs will 403 or miss data.

gotchas.title: Owner's Premium must stay active
gotchas.detail: If the owner's Premium lapses, the app stops working for everyone until they resubscribe.

gotchas.title: `localhost` redirect URIs are rejected
gotchas.detail: Use `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` or `http://[::1]:PORT`. Everything else must be HTTPS and match exactly.

gotchas.title: Refresh tokens hard-expire after 6 months
gotchas.detail: Refreshing does not extend the refresh token. Expect `invalid_grant` and plan for users to re-authorize about twice a year.

gotchas.title: Allowlisting is manual and email-exact
gotchas.detail: Community reports say you must add each user with the exact email on their Spotify account, and there is no API for it.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 403 with a message like 'User not registered in the Developer Dashboard' / 'user may not be registered'
blockers.fix: The account is not allowlisted. Add it under Users and Access (exact Spotify email). If you already have 5 users, you cannot add more without Extended Quota.

blockers.symptom: Authorize page shows 'INVALID_CLIENT: Invalid redirect URI' (wording per community reports)
blockers.fix: Register the exact redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. Use HTTPS, or a loopback IP literal for local testing; `localhost` is not accepted.

blockers.symptom: 403 or 404 on endpoints that worked before (e.g. `GET /playlists/{id}/tracks`, `GET /artists/{id}/top-tracks`, `GET /browse/new-releases`)
blockers.fix: Migrate to the February 2026 Development Mode endpoints (`/items`, `/me/library`, single-item fetches) or drop the feature. Only Extended Quota apps keep the old surface.

blockers.symptom: App suddenly stops working for all users
blockers.fix: Check that the app owner's Spotify Premium is active; the app resumes when Premium is restored.
The refresh token expired (6 months) or was revoked. Send the user through the auth flow again.

blockers.symptom: Extended Quota application declined or never answered
blockers.fix: Check you meet every criterion (registered business, 250k+ MAU, launched, key markets). If not, Spotify is not a viable multi-user integration; scope the product to the 5-user cap or drop it.

Whether sending Spotify metadata to an LLM at request time counts as 'ingesting Spotify Content into an AI model' under the Developer Terms; Spotify gives no guidance.

The exact Composio redirect URI for Spotify; the Composio Spotify page does not state it.
Real-world Extended Quota approval rates and response times after May 2025; Spotify only states 'up to six weeks'.

objects.name: User profile
objects.description: Current user's ID, display name, images and URI via GET /me
objects.note: Development Mode apps no longer get country, email, explicit_content, followers or product from GET /me since February 2026. GET /users/{id} for other users was removed.

objects.name: Playlists and playlist items
objects.description: The user's playlists and the tracks or episodes in them
objects.note: In Development Mode, /tracks became /items, and items are returned only for playlists the user owns or collaborates on. Other playlists return metadata only or 403. GET /users/{id}/playlists was removed; use GET /me/playlists.

objects.name: Saved library
objects.description: Saved tracks, albums, episodes and shows
objects.note: Reading saved tracks still works with user-library-read. Writes moved to PUT/DELETE /me/library with Spotify URIs, and per-type /contains checks moved to GET /me/library/contains.

objects.name: Recently played
objects.description: Tracks the user played recently, with played_at timestamps
objects.note: Does not include podcast episodes. Spotify does not document how far back the history goes.

objects.name: Top artists and tracks
objects.description: The user's most-played artists and tracks over about 4 weeks, 6 months or 1 year

objects.name: Playback state and control
objects.description: Current track, device and progress; start, pause, skip and transfer playback
objects.note: Reading state needs only the read scopes. Control endpoints work only for users with Spotify Premium.

changes.detail: Spotify's Web API docs describe no webhooks or push events, so you must poll. For listening history, poll GET /me/player/recently-played with the after cursor (a Unix ms timestamp) to fetch only new plays. For playlists and library, re-read and diff. Composio-managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval, but Spotify has no managed app on Composio, so you already use your own app and can poll faster where the toolkit supports it.

limits.text: Rate limits are counted over a rolling 30-second window per app. Over the limit you get HTTP 429, normally with a Retry-After header in seconds. Development Mode limits are much lower than Extended Quota limits; Spotify does not publish exact numbers.
Recently played, saved tracks, top items and playlist items return at most 50 per page (default 20). Page with offset, or with before/after cursors for recently played.

For Development Mode apps, search limit max dropped from 50 to 10 (default 5), and batch fetches like GET /tracks were removed. Fetching many items now costs one request each, which burns rate limit faster.

restrictions.text: Developer Terms Section IV.2.a.1 forbid training an ML or AI model on Spotify Content or otherwise ingesting it into one. Spotify gives no guidance on whether passing data to an LLM at request time counts.

You may not build databases or compilations of Spotify Content, or store it indefinitely. Local caching is allowed only as strictly necessary for performance; metadata and cover art may be cached temporarily.
Keep displayed data reasonably current. Delete a user's personal data within 5 days after they disconnect, and all Spotify Content if your access ends.
